subject: Coord: Intercom, Zendesk & Gainsight renewals — timeline & negotiation
messages:
From: Amy Liu <amy@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Support stack renewal windows and questions

Hi Vanessa,

We’re starting our renewal planning for the customer support stack and I wanted to align timelines with Redwood. Our Intercom and Zendesk contracts both renew in March, and Gainsight renews at the end of April. Before we pull procurement in, a few quick questions:

- Can Redwood provide a single consolidated renewal MOP (mutual action plan) that covers all three vendors?
- What flexibility do you have on staggered cutovers vs. a single consolidated migration window?
- Any info on standard concession ranges / pilot discounts you’ve offered for multi-product renewals recently?

We’ve attached our internal renewal calendar (not included in this thread). Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Amy Liu
Director, Customer Experience
Acme Retail
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Liu <amy@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support stack renewal windows and questions

Hi Amy — thanks for the heads up and the timeline.

Short answers up front: yes, we can produce a consolidated mutual action plan that covers hosted API + Dedicated/Private routing considerations; and we’ve handled both staggered and consolidated cutovers depending on the customer’s risk appetite. Concessions are negotiable but depend on committed volumes (tokens/seat licenses) and whether you consolidate billing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal alignment call at Redwood (30 min) to confirm negotiation bands and legal asks — Thurs 1/14 10:00am PT or Fri 1/15 1:00pm PT.
2) Draft a single MOP template for Acme that lists milestones per product and a suggested combined timeline.
3) Share a short concession/pricing summary for each product (Zendesk, Intercom, Gainsight) — will include typical ranges and pilot options.

I’m attaching our standard RFP response doc for renewals (Acme_Renewal_RFP_2027.pdf).

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme renewal negotiation framework

Folks — recapping what I want to bring to the alignment call:

- Commercial floor/ceiling per product: Intercom (pilot discount 10–20%, full renewal concessions up to 25% bundled), Zendesk (typically 5–15% unless moving to enterprise tier), Gainsight (discounts driven by seat count and product modules; 15% typical for renewals with a new committed ARR).
- Key non-negotiables: no cross-product data residency variance without legal OK; SLA language changes go to Legal and Infra for signoff.
- Ask for Acme: single POC contact, expected cutover risk tolerance (low/medium/high), and whether they require dedicated capacity or private deployment for any product.

Attached a draft pricing workbook for internal use (Gainsight_pricing_sheet.xlsx) and a short concessions summary I used last quarter (Intercom_concession_summary.docx).

For the call, I’ll propose an authority matrix: who can approve up to X% concession without legal escalation. My suggestion: up to 12% — CS/APX can approve; 12–20% requires Sales Leader; >20% requires Revenue Ops/Legal.

Ben Carter
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Liu <amy@acme.com>, Erik Johansson <erik@clearwater.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support stack renewal windows and questions

Hi Amy, Erik — appreciate the timeline. Per our internal review, here’s a proposed consolidated approach for Acme:

- Phase 1 (Mar): Intercom — apply pilot discount (15%) and change order for conversational routing to reduce duplicate tickets. Goal: lower MTTI.
- Phase 2 (Apr): Zendesk — standard renewal, offer 10% bundle discount if you commit to consolidated billing and a 12-month paid pilot for two integrations.
- Phase 3 (May): Gainsight — renew with product module review; offer a one-time implementation credit (covers CSM onboarding hours) if they sign by 4/15.

I’ve created a short MOP with milestones and owner names; we can push the DocuSign envelope for a bundled agreement once Acme confirms. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/preview/abc123

Questions for you both:
- Would Acme prefer one consolidated contract or three separate agreements with a master services addendum?
- Who will be the procuring contact from Acme (name/email) and expected procurement timeline?

If you’re available, Vanessa and I can do a joint call Thursday 1/21 to finalize the MOP.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 617-555-0243
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Finalize Acme concession limits + legal route

Quick internal note after Marissa’s outreach — Acme is leaning toward a consolidated agreement but wants separate product SOWs under that master agreement. Action items: 

1) Ben — confirm final concession ceilings for each product by EOD Friday 1/22 so I can reflect numbers in the MOP.
2) Karthik — please loop in Legal and Revenue Ops; confirm whether the master + SOW approach is acceptable and what SLA language we must preserve.
3) Marissa — draft the one-page MOP timeline we’ll send to Amy; include milestone owners and the proposed sign-by date of 2027-04-15 to lock Gainsight credits.

If we keep the concessions within the thresholds Ben outlined (<20% bundled), we can approve without escalation. If Acme asks for >20% on any line, I’ll push for countervalue (commitment, multi-year, or onboarding fee).

I’ll own the customer call scheduling once Ben and Karthik confirm.

—Vanessa
